purpose: Refine DENSITY_THRESHOLD_BEFORE_ORCHESTRATION and FLEXIBILITY_CALLABILITY_GATE: raw actor count or stated interest is insufficient. A shared node becomes economically callable only when enough compatible, recurring and sufficiently committed workload exists to cover fixed coordination/capability cost. This is not a new ontology or shared-service business thesis.

evidence: Xuzhou has more than 140 customized bus routes and provides regular commuting service to more than 85 enterprises/institutions.
Enterprise routes are designed from employee residential distribution, commute peaks and route preferences, rather than raw employee count.

Public reporting says enterprise demand is stable and willingness to pay is strong; annual enterprise commuting service exceeds 2 million passenger trips and the operator locks long-term stable ridership.
findings.interpretation: The shared route is supported by repeatable paid load with compatible origin/destination/time structure. Potential riders alone would not create the route.

evidence: Guannan integrates actual flight requirements from 11 townships and 19 departments into one shared-operation system.
Participating units purchase flight services on demand rather than each owning drones, training pilots and maintaining fleets.
Public reporting says the unified shared model reduces single-flight cost by more than 60%.
findings.interpretation: A callable shared drone capability emerged from real task flow that can be centrally scheduled, not from generic institutional interest in drones.

evidence: Binhai Green-Island intelligent manufacturing service center centralizes high-investment/high-pollution downstream processes such as spraying.
Its spraying center processes more than 6 million parts per year for local enterprises.
findings.interpretation: The node is supported by measurable recurring compatible throughput large enough to amortize fixed equipment, governance and environmental-control cost. A list of firms that might need spraying would not be equivalent evidence.

evidence: XCMG exposes intelligent welding capability and has co-built a shared welding center with more than 30 local SMEs.
The underlying system is a specific production capability with measurable weld quality and efficiency improvements, not a generic expert-sharing pool.
findings.interpretation: Thirty firms matter only because sufficiently compatible welding tasks can be routed through a common capability and acceptance interface. Raw SME count is not the economic density.

evidence: Bus demand must align in geography and time.
Drone demand must be expressible as schedulable flight tasks.
Shared manufacturing demand must fit common process specifications.
Shared laboratory and waste-collection systems from earlier scans likewise require compatible test classes or waste categories rather than raw actor count.
findings.interpretation: Economic density is compatibility-weighted and commitment-weighted. Heterogeneous or hypothetical demand should not be summed as if fungible.

evidence: Issue #143 already distinguishes interest from economic commitment at the single-exchange level.
Shared-node evidence shows the same rule at system scale: prospective users do not finance fixed capability; recurring accepted task volume does.
findings.interpretation: The project should use the same epistemic discipline at both levels: INTEREST != COMMITMENT and POTENTIAL_VOLUME != BASELOAD.

search_rules_refined.name: BASELOAD_COMMITMENT_GATE
questions: What recurring task volume already occurs, rather than might occur?
Who actually pays, orders, schedules or commits that volume?
What fixed capability/coordination cost must the baseline load cover?
What minimum frequency or throughput keeps the node economically viable?
Can one anchor buyer, route, contract or workload cover the fixed floor while long-tail actors add utilization?
search_rules_refined.relationship_to_existing_doctrine: Refinement of DENSITY_THRESHOLD_BEFORE_ORCHESTRATION and FLEXIBILITY_CALLABILITY_GATE; not a new top-level ontology.

search_rules_refined.name: COMPATIBILITY_WEIGHTED_DENSITY
questions: Are the tasks compatible enough to share the same equipment, specialist, route, standard, time window or acceptance interface?
What fraction of observed demand is actually fungible/routable through the same node?
Does heterogeneity create setup/changeover/translation/quality cost that destroys the apparent density?

search_rules_refined.name: ANCHOR_LOAD_WITHOUT_FALSE_DEMAND
questions: Is there a named actor with recurring accepted demand?
Is the anchor relationship already evidenced by purchase/service/contract/operational use rather than stated interest?
Would the shared node still survive if speculative long-tail demand disappeared?
search_rules_refined.boundary: An anchor is evidence of baseline economics only; it does not prove a scalable market or profitability.
